what: Vocal production architectures and chop behaviour. chops is read by the chop games (games: the hook and lines answering in builds and tails; sparse: hook teasers only; stutter: the roll into the last drop only; none). The chain and send layouts are applied with apply_fx_chain, create_send_route and add_automation_clip after the build. The person's rule stands in every option: chops are whole phrases at their own pitch.

options.label: Chop games: hook teasers, answers, tail games, stutter roll
options.what: The current default: the hook teased in the intro, a line and the hook traded in builds, 8 bars of games after each chorus, a stutter roll into the last drop.

sources.where: Laurie Webb vocal chops as the drop's lead

options.label: Sparse: the hook once in the intro, nothing between choruses
options.what: The singer is the record: whole verses and choruses, the hook chop only as an intro teaser and in the outro. No chop games over the instrumental parts, which keep their own melody.

sources.where: lead vocal over the loop, no chops
two vocal channels, dub sends doing the work

options.label: Lead, doubles left and right, harmonies, texture bus
options.what: The vocal as an arrangement: the lead centre, two doubles panned, an ambient double, a distorted 'robot' double, high, mid and low harmonies, hums and 'oh's, ad-libs, each family on its bus (Lead, Doubles, Harmonies, Vocal Texture, Adlib) and one shared reverb.

sources.where: Lead, Doubles L/R, Ambient double, Robot double (Blood Overdrive), High/Mid/Low harmonies, hums, ad-libs; buses Lead, Doubles, Harmonies, Vocal Texture, Adlib; LuxeVerb send

options.manual: Doubles from the record's own double track when the stems have one; otherwise a Pitcher harmony a third and a fifth up at -12 dB, panned 60 % left and right.

options.label: Reggaeton stack: Main, Duo, Trio, Low, High, Far
options.what: One lead recorded into seven inserts with their own jobs: Main (dry, forward), Duo and Trio (thickening doubles), Low and High (Pitcher harmonies an octave and a third away), Separated (panned), Far (a delay-and-reverb only send), plus filtered radio ad-libs on their own delay.

sources.where: inserts Main, Duo, Trio, Low, Separated, High, Far with Pitcher and Pitch Shifter formant, vocal delay sends

options.label: Melodic techno vocal: pitched, widened, gated reverb, it ducks the leads
options.what: The vocal tuned (Pitcher), formant moved by automation, widened on two parallel buses (Spreader plus Hyper Chorus), its reverb gated by Gross Beat and ducked under the next line; the vocal itself ducks the lead synths by a Peak Controller.

sources.where: Pitch Shifter > EQ > Pitcher > Maximus > Peak Controller; Stereo Vocal and Vocal Widness buses; Vocal Reverb with Gross Beat Gate; Reverb Shimmer

options.label: Drill: lead bus, driven ad-lib bus, hook stabs, quarter and half delays
options.what: The lead vocal clean and compressed hard on its bus, ad-libs on a bus that adds Blood Overdrive, the hook doubled as short 'stabs', two tempo delays (a quarter for verses, a half for the hook) and one reverb; pan offset thrown left and right on single words.

sources.where: Lead Vocal Bus, Lead Vocal Adlib Bus (Blood Overdrive), Hook Stab Bus, REVERB, 1/4 DELAY, 1/2 DELAY; pan offset clips of 1.25 to 2 beats

options.label: Dub sends: delay and reverb rides, breath dips
options.what: The vocal stays dry and close; its delay (a delay bank into a reverb) and reverb sends are ridden by automation phrase by phrase, and the breaths are dipped by a volume clip. The space moves, the voice does not.

sources.where: Vocal Delay (Delay Bank > Reeverb 2) and Vocal Reverb sends automated over 228 beats, Dip Breath clips of 97 points

options.label: The whole vocal in order, its own hook as the only chop
options.what: Every sung line of the record kept whole and in its order, stretched to the remix tempo with its pitch and formants kept (FL: e3 Mono or Stretch pro with F.Shift at 0); no line is pitched, filtered, stuttered or re-cut. The only chops are the record's own hook (its vocal-chop motif), teased in the intro and carrying the drops.

options.label: A dry, close verse voice against a wide, washed chorus voice
options.what: Two vocal spaces that never fight: the verse (a rap or a low spoken line) dry, mono and up front in the low mids; the chorus voice high-passed at about 220 Hz, through a chorus effect and a long reverb (about 25 ms pre-delay, 2.1 s decay) so it spreads to the edges. Hook teasers only in the chops.
